A.explanation: Nucleon number $A$ must stay at $10$ in $\beta^{+}$ decay, so $^{11}_{6}\text{C}$ with $A=11$ cannot be formed.

B.explanation: Nucleon number $A$ must stay at $10$ in $\beta^{+}$ decay, so $^{9}_{6}\text{C}$ with $A=9$ cannot be formed.

C.explanation: In $\beta^{+}$ decay $A$ is unchanged at $10$ and $Z$ decreases by $1$ from $6$ to $5$, giving $^{10}_{5}\text{B}$.

D.explanation: In $\beta^{+}$ decay a proton is lost, so $Z$ decreases by $1$ and cannot increase from $6$ to $7$ as in $^{10}_{7}\text{N}$.

hints: Notice the parent $^{10}_{6}\text{C}$ has nucleon number $A = 10$ and proton number $Z = 6$.
Recall the $\beta^{+}$ change inside the nucleus: a proton becomes a neutron plus a positron and a neutrino.
Check how $A$ and $Z$ must change to conserve nucleon number and charge, then compare $^{11}_{6}\text{C}$, $^{9}_{6}\text{C}$, $^{10}_{5}\text{B}$ and $^{10}_{7}\text{N}$.
walkthrough: Identify the parent nuclide: $^{10}_{6}\text{C}$ means $A = 10$ total nucleons and $Z = 6$ protons.
State the $\beta^{+}$ rule: one proton converts to one neutron, emitting a positron $^{0}_{+1}\text{e}$ and a neutrino.
Apply nucleon conservation: one nucleon remains one nucleon, so $A$ is unchanged and stays at $10$.
Apply charge and proton-number change: losing one proton means $Z$ decreases by $1$, so $Z = 6 - 1 = 5$.
Form the daughter nuclide with $A = 10$ and $Z = 5$, which is boron $^{10}_{5}\text{B}$. This is option C.
